summary: Package ships a Linux native addon that harvests browser credentials on require()
details: The package contains no JavaScript source and a 107-byte README. Its package.json points `main` at a 10 MB Linux ELF native addon (`tools.linux-x64-gnu.node`), so any consumer that `require()`s the package loads and runs the addon's N-API init at import time. Extracted strings from the ELF show a Rust build embedding SQLite (including `SQLITE_AUTH_USER`), the `ureq` HTTP client with `rustls` TLS, host fingerprinting primitives (`getifaddrs`, `gethostname`, reads of `/etc/lsb-release`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`, `bogomips per cpu`, `network_adapters`), and log-message fragments specific to browser secret extraction (`Found login for `, ` on Cookie.value when inserting `). The combination of SQLite access, an HTTPS client, host-identification syscalls, and browser login/cookie log strings is the standard shape of a browser-credential stealer that reads Chromium `Login Data`/`Cookies` SQLite databases and exfiltrates the results. Package metadata reinforces the burner-publish shape: a platform-suffixed generic name with no repository, no homepage, no author provenance, and a nonsensical version `3.1.40-chrom-468-delete-windows-32-bit-358-1784544836` containing keyword noise and a trailing Unix-timestamp-shaped integer typical of automated batch publication.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
